newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo stocks end higher on select buying.
newsitem.headline: Colombo stocks end higher on select buying.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed slightly higher on Friday as investors bought shares of companies which showed higher profits for 1996, brokers said.
The all share index closed 0.9 points up at 620.5. Shares of Distilleries Company closed 50 cents up at 7.50 and those of Colombo Dockyard Ltd one rupee higher at 15.

"Investors focused on companies which had seen good corporate growth in 1996," said Sanjeeva Gunewardena, a trader at Ceylinco Securities. "Buyers paid premiums to get these stocks because a month from now they would probably be trading at higher prices," he added.
But overall sentiment remains cautious ahead of March 21 local government elections, brokers said.
Turnover was 16.5 million rupees on 1.02 million shares. The main trades were 15,000 shares of Ceylon Tobacco, 550,000 of Distilleries and 55,800 of Colombo Dockyard.
Foreign buying was 6.2 million and selling was 5.2 million.
"With elections round the corner, the overall market will remain in a tight range on low volumes," said Dimuthu Abeysekera, a trader at Allied Phillips Securities.
